parts:
Dear Listers,

I have what must be a regularly occuring desire to use a wider data set t=
o calculate a detction function and then impose the function onto subsets=
of the data with much smaller sample sizes. We reason that our species w=
ill remain as detctable between years as long as we hold the seasons simi=
lar.=20

Now I have found this page in the help file for Distance 6.0 Release 2, "=
Using a previopusly fitted detection function to Estimate Density in MRDS=
". It describes switching off the removal of new objects in R which seems=
straight forward enough. However after that, the instructions appear to =
depart from the reality of the windows observed.

This part of the helpfile is particularly problematic. "Now we=E2=80=99ll=
apply this detection function to the new subset of data. Define a new da=
ta filter that selects the new subset of data. Note that it must be a sub=
set of the data used to fit the detection function. Define a new Model De=
finition, and in the Estimate tab, check the option to Estimate density /=
abundance and also the option to Use the fitted detection function from =
previous MRDS analysis. Select the ID of the analysis you want to use. Fo=
r example, if you want to use analysis 2 (called =E2=80=9CFI - MR dist=E2=
=80=9D in this case), the lower half of the Estimate tab will look like t=
his: Applying the fitted detection function from one analysis to another =
analysis"

I cannot locate or stimulate the appearance of the "Use the fitted functi=
on from previous MRDS analysis". Am I doing something very wrong?=20

Best, Graham Hemson

messages.subject: Re: Applying a global or previously used detection function
parts:
Graham:

The passage that you found in the users guide describes using the=20
mark-recapture distance sampling engine. So you will need to be using=20
the MRDS engine to fit your detection function to your data for the=20
remainder of that section of the guide to be useful to you. Are you=20
indeed using MRDS for your detection function fitting?
